concepts.notes: Require the latent-attention path, not just fewer KV heads.
Routed experts must be present; active and stored parameters remain separate.
A window value alone does not establish the per-layer schedule.
Specific DeepSeek sparse/indexed-MLA path; generic sparse attention is not automatically DSA.
Normalization of queries/keys; this does not determine the decoder normalization algorithm.
Retain per-path settings and partial rotary scope. Do not assume that every path uses RoPE.
The published activation must say SiLU/Swish; SiTU-GLU is a different claim.
Scope to the MLA path described by mla_use_nope. Missing RoPE metadata never establishes NoPE.
Output gating only; a gated FFN or sigmoid router is not proof of gated attention.
Use an explicit site definition: attention combined with linear/recurrent/state-space/convolution mixers. Mixing local/global softmax alone is not this category.
Distinguish standalone decoder mixer layers from the short convolution inside KDA. Never add the nested operation to the decoder layer sum.
Block attention-residual setting is retained. Preserve its source and block scope; do not infer it from a generic residual multiplier.
Published expert latent width and routed expert pool support a latent expert path.
Only positive module counts/parameters. A zero-layer setting does not mean the model contains MTP; keep module counts separate from the decoder total.
Existing structured field occurs only in a held record. Shared index selection is not the same as shared KV cache.
Shared-layer loops and their per-loop cache semantics are present only in a held record.
Family-specific kind is retained only in a held record; indexer dimensions, micro-block selection and cache semantics still need qualification.
No published normalization-type field. rms_norm_eps and norm tensor names are useful leads, not proof of the normalization equation.
ple_embed_dim is present in the pinned Qwen config but is not consumed into a checked concept fact. Do not reinterpret n-gram memory as per-layer embedding.
Compression ratios are retained in primary configs, but extraction collapses the mechanism to an unsupported compressed-attention kind. Add distinct compression/selection and per-layer rules.
hyper_connection_multiplier is too generic. The pinned DeepSeek config also has Sinkhorn settings; validate the constrained mixing implementation before calling it mHC.
Pinned configs contain indexer_types or index_source_layer_ids, but the extractor has no checked index-sharing schedule. Keep index reuse separate from KV reuse.
The Qwen card describes this, while extraction retains only a generic hyper-connection count. Read and verify the read/write gate semantics independently of mHC.
No qualified field or representative recorded family. Define whether the budget is per layer/head, static/dynamic, and training/inference before adding a rule.
